The aggravating structural point is also verified: KLC §10 hook D enforces "Criteria of §9 met" — the kernel is required to enforce a predicate whose security-bearing terms no document defines, and which CI never exercises. §11.2 makes an affirmative claim ("This closes the single-compromised-source poisoning path") that an undefined independence relation cannot support; B14's original defeat (three sessions each reading the same poisoned document) remains available verbatim.

5. The redesign-built-the-substrate observation is accurate: §3.1 moves per-operator session/conversation state and the memory recall index into the queryable state store, and §6.3 adds `tier`, `tier_ceiling`, provenance/lineage to those rows — precisely the material a lineage-disjointness / distinct-issuer check would query. Nothing is wired to it.

Refutation attempts that failed: (a) "the corpus addresses it elsewhere" — it does not; the only other mention is §14 Q8 declaring it undecided and the autopsy §131 noting it remains open. (b) "YAGNI / rough-design deferral legitimately excludes it" — a deferral would be legitimate if the corpus did not simultaneously assert the poisoning path is closed (§11.2) and require the kernel to adjudicate the gate (hook D). Deny-by-default doctrine also cuts the other way: an undefined predicate at an enforcement hook is the opposite of deny-by-default. (c) "§12's spine is only a label/DCS conformance spine, so promotion gates were never in scope" — this is the strongest available refutation, but it fails on the document's own words: §12 explicitly enrolls "KLC §15 invariants" as vectors, i.e. the spine does claim lifecycle-invariant coverage, and D15 calls it the *single* spine. The gap is therefore inside the claimed scope, not outside it.

Where I would trim the finding: the recommendation's specific floor (distinct registry issuers, disjoint lineage closures, no common non-Tier-≤1 ancestor) is one reasonable design, not the only one, and asserting it now partially pre-empts Q8's actual question (same-peer-domain vs. cross-domain). The defensible half of the recommendation is the mechanical part the finding itself frames correctly: state a floor as a §15 invariant so it enters the spine, and change the §9.1 parenthetical from a citation-of-a-definition to an honest "(independence: OPEN — §14 Q8)". The current parenthetical is the sharper defect, because it reads as if a definition exists.

findings.section: §15 control map preamble ('delta over the KLC §13 and ADR mappings')
findings.rl1_disposition: open — new instance of RL#1's Class B (two-representations drift). RL#1's remedy ADR-0006 is scoped to the KLC §10 hook table + §15 invariants, ADR-owned decision status, regenerated diagrams, and inherited-vs-extended labelling; it does not name the security-control-mapping tables, so as drafted it would not kill the class at this seam. This is not a redesign that relocated the class — it is a seam RL#1's enumeration did not reach. ADR-0006's single-source-of-truth scope should be widened to include the control map (assemble the RMF matrix from one source).
findings.relocated_class: Class B — two-representations drift, relocated from intra-document (KLC §10 hook table / §15 invariants / §6 prose) to inter-document control-mapping tables (KLC §13 / ABAC §15 / ADR-0003 mapping table). Same structural shape: N tables restating the same facts that must stay in sync.
findings.summary: The table declares itself a delta but at least three rows restate KLC §13 rows verbatim or near-verbatim, creating a second copy of the same control mappings — and because the AC-16(6) error now sits in both tables, the corpus has demonstrated the failure mode live: one wrong row, two places to fix.
findings.evidence: Duplicated: the Bell-LaPadula row (identical AC-3(3)/AC-4/AC-16(6) set), the label-binding row (identical AC-16/SC-16), and the RLS row re-using §13's AC-3/CM-7/SC-7 for a different element.
findings.recommendation: Make §15 a true delta: state that KLC §13 and the ADR tables are canonical for the elements they cover and restrict §15 to rows with no §13 antecedent (state store/RLS, OAuth front door, OpenTDF, boot validation, conformance vectors); replace the BLP and label-binding rows with pointers. Longer term, assemble the RMF matrix from one source rather than three tables that must agree.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
Verified directly against the text. ABAC §15 declares itself a "Delta over the KLC §13 and ADR mappings — rows specific to this document," but two rows are not deltas: the Bell-LaPadula row (abac-dcs-architecture.md:330, `AC-3(3), AC-4, AC-16(6)`) is control-for-control identical to knowledge-lifecycle-contract.md:247, and the label-binding row (abac:331, `AC-16, SC-16`) is identical to KLC:246.

The finding's third example is REFUTED as stated: the RLS row (abac:333, `AC-3, SC-7 (internal boundary), CM-7`) is not a restatement of KLC:245 (`AC-3, AC-6, CM-7`) — different element, different set; reusing a control across distinct elements is normal RMF practice, not a second representation. So the count is two, not "at least three."

The finding UNDERSTATES the shape elsewhere, however: ADR-0003:35 maps deny-by-default to `AC-3, AC-6, CM-7`, a third copy of KLC §13's row 1, and ABAC §15's three-layer-enforcement row restates `AC-3, AC-4, AC-6`. The corpus genuinely has three tables that must agree.

The live-failure claim holds: AC-16(6) sits in both tables, and design/reviews/RL1-findings-digest.json carries a NIST-text-verified finding that AC-16(6) is the wrong enhancement (it requires individual users rather than the system to maintain attribute associations, the opposite of Maknae's system-stamped, gate-verified labels). One wrong mapping, two correction sites — the failure mode is demonstrated, not hypothetical.

Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "the BLP rows describe different elements (contract-level rule vs three-layer enforcement)" — the element wording differs cosmetically but the control set is byte-identical, so the row carries zero delta information; (2) "both tables are marked (informative) and defer to the RMF package as canonical" — true and it caps blast radius, but a self-declared delta that isn't one is a factual defect regardless of normativity; (3) YAGNI/deny-by-default doctrine does not excuse it — this violates the corpus's own READ-reality doctrine restated in RL#1 §3.

Severity held at should-fix rather than raised: the demonstrated duplicated error lifts it above nit, but both tables are informative, only 2 of 11 rows duplicate, and the AC-16(6) correctness error itself is already tracked separately. The fix (replace duplicated rows with pointers; declare KLC §13 + ADR tables canonical for elements they cover) is cheap and mechanical.

findings.rl1_disposition: open — RL#1 named control-mapping accuracy as a genuine finding family (review line 25) and recorded that Codex surfaced "several control-mapping scope errors" (line 134) without enumerating rows. No redesign or correction has been applied to §15 or KLC §13, so the class is carried forward and newly instanced with specific rows. Not killed; not relocated (no redesign occurred that could relocate it).
findings.summary: Multiple §15 rows carry control ids derived from control-family recall rather than the control text — AC-16(6), SC-3, IA-2 (twice), PT-2 on the hashing row, SI-10 (twice), SC-7/CM-7 on the RLS row — while the on-point controls (AC-16(9)/(2)/(3), AC-25, SC-3(2), AC-16(7), IA-9, SI-19/SI-12, SC-24, SA-8(24), SA-11(1)/(8), AC-3(3), AC-24) are absent.
findings.evidence: Verified against SP 800-53r5: AC-16(6) requires PERSONNEL (not the system) to maintain attribute associations — the inverse of Maknae's derived-only, kernel-stamped labels, and it is now wrong in two documents. SC-3 isolates security from NONsecurity functions, so 'decision isolated from enforcement' is not its subject (the real SC-3 story is trust plane vs runtime plane), and AC-25 REFERENCE MONITOR — which AC-3(3)'s own discussion names as the required basis and which the 'kernel is the only PDP' claim needs — appears nowhere. IA-2 does not cover attribute sourcing (row 2) and is largely inherited from the federated IdP (row 3), with non-person scoped task identities needing IA-9. PT-2 is an organizational authority-to-process determination, not a de-identification control (SI-19/SI-12 are). SI-10 is information input validation, not configuration integrity or CI test vectors (CM-6(2), SC-24, SA-8(24), SA-11 enhancements are). SC-7/CM-7 on an RLS row is boundary protection and least functionality applied to access enforcement, behind a parenthetical hedge ('internal boundary') that concedes the reach.
findings.recommendation: Re-derive each row from the control text rather than family recall, applying the specific substitutions above, and fix KLC §13's copy in the same change. Adopt one corpus-wide hedging convention (an explicit 'supports, does not implement' column) so parenthetical concessions survive transcription into the RMF matrix.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
Verified row-by-row against abac-dcs-architecture.md:327-337 and knowledge-lifecycle-contract.md:245-252.

CONFIRMED, strongest first:
1. AC-16(6) (line 330 + KLC:247) — AC-16(6) is "Attribute Association by Organization," requiring PERSONNEL to associate/maintain attribute associations. Maknae's labels are derived and kernel-stamped, i.e. AC-16(3) (Maintenance of Attribute Associations by System); the no-automated-downgrade claim is AC-16(9) (Regrading Mechanisms). The cited control is the inverse of the design, and it is duplicated verbatim across two documents (also a Class-B two-representations instance).
2. SC-3 (line 327) — the parenthetical gloss "security function isolation — decision isolated from enforcement" misstates the control's subject: SC-3 isolates security from NONsecurity functions. PDP and PEP are both security functions; SC-3(2) is the enhancement that isolates access/flow-control functions from OTHER security functions. AC-25 (Reference Monitor) is absent corpus-wide despite the tamperproof/always-invoked/analyzable "kernel is the only PDP" thesis.
3. IA-2 (line 328) — identification/authentication of organizational users; says nothing about attribute sourcing from a signed authoritative store. Confirmed mismatch. Additional unlisted instance of the same class: KLC:252 maps scheduler/dreaming-cycle scoped (non-person, service) identities to IA-2, where IA-9 is on point.
4. PT-2 on the hashing/zero-PII audit row (line 334, propagated from prose at line 255 "the MCP's PT-2/AU-10 pattern verbatim") — PT-2 is Authority to Process PII, an organizational determination, not de-identification (SI-19/SI-12). Line 335's PT-2 for "privacy regimes" is the one loosely defensible use.
5. SC-7/CM-7 on the RLS row (line 332) — boundary protection and least functionality applied to intra-database row filtering; the source text's own "(internal boundary)" hedge concedes the reach, which is exactly the transcription-survival problem the recommendation targets.

WEAKER than the finding presents:
- Line 329 IA-2 for the OAuth 2.1 front door is defensible on its face; the objection there is an inheritance-boundary quibble, not a scope error.
- SI-10 (lines 333, 337) is a stretch but arguable (config files as inputs). Notably, BOTH the doc and the finding miss the most on-point control for boot-time validation with fail-to-start: SI-6 (Security and Privacy Function Verification — verify at startup, shut down on anomaly), with SC-24 secondary.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: (a) §15 is headed "(informative)" and closes "Full matrix belongs in the RMF package, not this document" — this lowers stakes but does not license inverted control semantics, and these rows are the seed corn for the real matrix; (b) no other corpus location corrects these ids — the KLC §13 copy repeats rather than fixes; (c) nothing in the YAGNI/deny-by-default doctrine excuses citing a control whose text states the opposite of the design.

findings.summary: DoDI 8520.04 has no paragraph 3.4 — Section 3 contains only 3.1 and 3.2 — so the '§3.4, §4.3' citation is wrong in both places it appears; the correct anchors for the claim made are §4.2.d, §4.3 and the Glossary definition of dynamic access.
findings.evidence: Verified against the lake's authoritative copy (852004p.md, DoDI 8520.04 of 3 Sep 2024). The substance is accurate: the Glossary defines dynamic access, §4.2 states it does not require provisioning entitlements, and §4.2.d requires reliance only on attribute services operated per §4.3. Only the pinpoint is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Replace '§3.4, §4.3' with '§4.2.d, §4.3 (and the Glossary definition of dynamic access)' in both §2.1 and §15.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE AUTHORITATIVE TEXT (lake copy /Users/thaChuck/_devops/projects/mpe-es/github-mpe-es/knowledgebase/852004p.md, DoDI 8520.04, 3 Sep 2024).

Defect confirmed. Section 3 of DoDI 8520.04 contains exactly two paragraphs — "3.1. IT AND DIGITAL RESOURCE PROTOCOL." (line 779) and "3.2. SYSTEM PROTOCOL." (line 796). Section 4 runs 4.1–4.5 (lines 869, 1027, 1265, 1328, 1383). There is no paragraph 3.4. The citation "§3.4, §4.3" is therefore a dangling pinpoint.

Both occurrence sites confirmed in /Users/thaChuck/_devops/peers/ack-darkhonor/maknae/design/abac-dcs-architecture.md:
- line 35, inside §2.1 "Zero Trust / ABAC policy stack" (header at line 28): "...attributes only from authoritative attribute services (§3.4, §4.3)"
- line 328, inside §15 "Security control mapping (informative)" (header at line 321): "DoDI 8520.04 §3.4/§4.3 alignment"

Substance of the claim is accurate, as the finding says: Glossary G.2 (line 1584) defines "dynamic access" as "The process of determining authorization when the entity requests…"; §4.2.b (line 1198) states dynamic access is determined at request time from the digital policy rule and user/environment attribute values and "does not require provisioning entitlements or accounts for the user"; §4.3 (line 1265) sets the authoritative attribute service requirements. So only the pinpoint is wrong — the finding's characterization holds.

CORRECTION TO THE FINDING'S RECOMMENDATION (do not apply it as written). The finding proposes replacing "§3.4, §4.3" with "§4.2.d, §4.3". There is no §4.2.d either — §4.2 has only "a. Explicit Access" (line 1029) and "b. Dynamic Access" (line 1198). The requirement the design doc is actually invoking ("attributes only from authoritative attribute services") is **§3.2.d** (line 809): "When implementing dynamic access, system owners must only rely on attributes provided by attribute services operated in accordance with Paragraph 4.3." That is almost certainly what "§3.4" was a typo/mis-transcription of. Applying the finding's literal recommendation would swap one dangling pinpoint for another.

Correct replacement: **§3.2.d, §4.2.b, §4.3 (and the Glossary definition of "dynamic access")** — or minimally "§3.2.d, §4.3" to preserve the original two-anchor shape.

Refutation attempts that failed: (i) the citation is not defensible as a reference to a different edition — the doc explicitly scopes it to "Access Management, Sep 2024", which is the copy verified; (ii) it is not saved by §2.1 being an informative summary table, since §15 repeats the same pinpoint in a control-mapping table whose whole purpose is assessor-facing traceability; (iii) nothing elsewhere in the corpus supplies the correct anchor — grep for "8520.04" across design/ returns only these two pinpointed sites plus two prose mentions (lines 99, 129) that carry no paragraph reference.

Secondary observation (not a separate finding): the same wrong pinpoint is duplicated verbatim at two sites. Today they agree, so this is a duplicated error rather than drift — but fixing one and not the other converts it into an instance of RL#1's Class B (two-representations drift). Fix both in the same edit.

Severity: should-fix, unchanged. It is more than a nit because §15 is the assessor-facing control-mapping table and the corpus's own recent practice makes security control mappings a required, auditable artifact (commits 5e76b96 / ce17246); a citation an assessor cannot resolve undermines the mapping's credibility. It is not a blocker because no enforcement mechanism, trust boundary, or design decision depends on the pinpoint — the underlying requirement is real and correctly characterized.

rl1_disposition: new. RL#1 (design/reviews/RL1-design-review-2026-07-14.md) collapses its 22 blockers into Class A (enforcement without a trust-plane locus) and Class B (two-representations drift); this is neither, and no 8520.04 citation issue appears in that review.

external_floor: false. This is a two-line text edit in a document under the authors' full control — a patchable seam, not an invariant outside the system.

findings.relocated_class: Not Class A. The Tier-0 store already sits in the trust plane, so no enforcement locus has escaped to the untrusted plane — the finding's "Class A adjacent" tag is a misfit. This belongs to the conformance / control-mapping-scope overclaim family that RL#1 §6 records as Codex-only should-fix signal ("several control-mapping scope errors"), and it has a Class B (two-representations) tail: the same claim is stated at strength in §2.1 line 35 and hedged as "alignment" in §15 line 328, and those two copies have already diverged. Genuinely new rather than relocated — abac-dcs-architecture.md is dated 2026-07-15 and did not exist when RL#1 ran on 2026-07-14 against container-architecture.md and the KLC.
findings.summary: Declaring the local Tier-0 signed store to BE 'the authoritative attribute service' exceeds DoDI 8520.04 §4.3, which requires DoD enterprise or Component approval, documented verification processes, published freshness, and (for person entities) DMDC EIAS as the authoritative source.
findings.evidence: Maknae's §4 attribute schema carries no verification-provenance or freshness fields. Structurally this is the shape the document forbids one level down: the platform self-declares its own store as authoritative exactly as it forbids a subject to self-assert attributes. The doctrinal point (identity is federated, attributes are not self-asserted) survives without the stronger claim.
findings.recommendation: Weaken to 'the Tier-0 signed store is Maknae's local attribute source of record; in a DoD deployment it is populated from — and traceable to — an approved authoritative attribute service per §4.3 (person-entity attributes from DMDC EIAS)'. Add verified_on / refresh_interval fields to the §4 schema and make stale-attribute handling a §9.2 row.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
I tried to refute this three ways and it survived all three.

**1. Is the external fact right?** Verified directly against the lake copy of the source, not memory: `/Users/thaChuck/_devops/projects/mpe-es/github-mpe-es/knowledgebase/852004p.md`. DoDI 8520.04 §4.3 says exactly what the finding claims:
- §4.3.a.(1)(a): "Authoritative attribute services must be approved for use at the DoD enterprise or DoD Component level…"
- §4.3.a.(2): "The authoritative source for person entity attributes is DMDC's 'DoD Enterprise Identity Attribute Service (EIAS) Person Entity Attribute Data Set Standard.'"
- §4.3.b (Accuracy): owners "must define and document the processes used to verify attribute values, including the frequency with which the attribute values are refreshed" and "must make freshness information (i.e., assertion of the last date the data was verified) available to organizations or system owners relying on the attributes."
- §5 adds a named sponsor/approval package process, with the approved list published at intelshare.intelink.gov.
Also confirmed §4.2 (line 1224): "System owners must obtain user attributes from approved authoritative attribute services as defined in Paragraph 4.3."

**2. Does the document actually make the claim?** Yes, flatly. `abac-dcs-architecture.md:35`, answer column: "…the Tier-0 signed attribute store + kernel binding **is the authoritative attribute service**." This is not hedged at the point of claim, and the §2.1 preamble explicitly raises the bar: "Verified against the operator's knowledge lake (2026-07-15), not model memory." §14's blanket "rough design binds to none of these documents' unread details" does NOT cover it — 8520.04 is absent from the §14 pending-references table precisely because it was treated as verified. §15's softer "DoDI 8520.04 §3.4/§4.3 alignment" (line 328) is a second, weaker representation of the same claim, so the corpus is not consistent with itself either.

**3. Is the corpus addressing it elsewhere / is the gap YAGNI-excluded?** No. §4's schema (lines 88-97) carries clearance / communities / nationality / handling_grants / roles and nothing else — no `verified_on`, no refresh interval, no feeder-system provenance, i.e. nothing that could satisfy §4.3.b's mandatory freshness assertion to relying parties. §9.2's fail-closed matrix has an "Attribute/registration drift at task fire time" row, but that is about a scheduled task's own re-evaluation, not staleness of the store's contents against an upstream source — there is no stale-attribute row. And this is demonstrably not a YAGNI exclusion: the corpus already knows the pattern one axis over — `knowledge-lifecycle-contract.md:87` gives *resource* objects a `freshness` field. Subject attributes are the axis that lacks it.

**Structural point, restated more precisely than the finding does.** The finding's framing ("self-declares authoritative exactly as it forbids a subject to self-assert") is a little loose — an operator-signed Tier-0 store is not a subject self-assertion, and §4.3.a.(1)(a) explicitly permits Component- or mission-partner-operated services, so Maknae's shape is not forbidden, it is merely unapproved-and-unattested as written. The sharper asymmetry is internal to §5.2 (line 129): the document already reasons "Maknae is never the Authorization Server: identity is not the platform's business, and DoDI 8520.04 wants authoritative sources" — it federates the identity half to an external locus and then terminates the attribute half inside itself, against the same instruction. That asymmetry is the real defect and it is visible in the text.

**Severity — independently re-assessed as should-fix, not blocker.** The actual security posture is sound (signed Tier-0, kernel-bound, no self-assertion); nothing is exploitable here. What is wrong is (a) a conformance claim a DoD assessor/AO would read as asserting an approval that does not exist, in a doc that flags the row as lake-verified, and (b) a real schema gap — §4.3.b freshness is a required *published* property, so satisfying it means adding fields to §4 and a stale-attribute row to §9.2, which is design-affecting rather than editorial. Not a nit. Not a blocker: §4.3.a.(1)(a)'s Component/mission-partner allowance means the fix is a scoping + traceability hedge plus two schema fields, not a redesign. The recommendation as written is well-aimed, and its "person-entity attributes from DMDC EIAS" clause is correctly sourced to §4.3.a.(2).

**One addition to the recommendation:** fix line 328's "§3.4/§4.3 alignment" in the same pass, or the weakened §2.1 row and the §15 control-mapping row become the corpus's own Class B two-representations drift on this exact fact.

It is, however, a fresh instance of RL#1's still-open **Class B (two-representations drift)** root class: the proposed ADR-0006 (corpus single-source-of-truth doctrine) has not been written — `design/adr/` holds only 0001–0003 — so the class that would have prevented this remains unaddressed and has now propagated into a new document. The document already demonstrates the correct discipline one row away — 'ACP 240 conformance claimed only after the document is in hand' — and applies it to nothing else, while D16 simultaneously promotes ACP 240 to normative guidance. §11's OpenTDF↔4778 equivalence is the riskiest: whether ZTDF assertion binding satisfies ADatP-4778's binding profiles is precisely what the unread text answers, and a wrong answer is expensive after the SDK API fossilizes. §14's STANAG row is also stale — nato-dcra-acp240-findings.md is in-repo with substantive 4774/4778/5636 material.
findings.recommendation: Scope the §2.1 preamble to the rows actually verified and mark the rest '(unverified)'; downgrade the STANAGs and ACP 240 from Authority/schema-ready to 'normative guidance, findings extract only, full text pending'; extend the ACP 240 hedge verbatim to 4774/4778/5636 and UIAS; relabel the UIAS deliverable a placeholder profile; move the OpenTDF↔4778 relationship to a §17 open question as a Phase-B gap analysis. Update §14's STANAG row to name the in-repo extract.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
CONFIRMED in its core, with one sub-claim refuted and part of the recommendation rejected.

WHAT SURVIVES (verified against text):

1. Blanket-vs-per-row verification claim. §2.1's preamble is unqualified: "Verified against the operator's knowledge lake (2026-07-15), not model memory:" — and it governs the whole table, including the "What it requires" cells (which are claims about document content). §14 then records ICTS UIAS v2.1 and "STANAG 4774 / 4778 / 5636 full texts" as "Not held". Two rows of a table asserted to be lake-verified cite authorities that are not in the lake. Genuine Class-B disagreement between copies of the same fact.

2. UIAS is the sharpest instance and is a flat contradiction. §4: "an **ICTS UIAS v2.1 mapping profile** ships for IC/enclave deployments" — a version-pinned deliverable against a vocabulary §14 marks "Not held", while §14's own lead sentence claims "Rough design binds to none of these documents' unread details". A v2.1 mapping profile is precisely a binding to that document's details. Note the doc gets the *provenance* discipline right here (§2.1 note + D6: UIAS is a profile, not the base standard) — the defect is the shipping commitment, not the citation.

3. "Schema-ready at MVP" for 4774/4778/5636 is an overclaim the repo's own material undercuts. The claimed evidence is one ported `label_id` placeholder column (§6.1). The in-repo extract (§4.1) shows ADatP-4774 is a full XML label syntax with policy OID and categories, and that NATO interposes a RESTRICTED level between UNCLASSIFIED and CONFIDENTIAL — flagged there as "a model change" — against Maknae's 5-level US-shaped classification ENUM. Readiness cannot be asserted for a syntax nobody has read; the material in hand actively suggests a lattice mismatch.

4. Hedge applied inconsistently. §2.1 demonstrates the correct discipline in the same cell ("ACP 240 conformance claimed only after the document is in hand") and extends it to nothing else in that row. The 800-162/205/8112 row is also correctly hedged ("full texts pending lake ingestion (§14) — final design re-walks them"), which makes the two unhedged authorities stand out as an omission rather than a house style.

5. §14's STANAG row IS stale. `references/nato-dcra-acp240-findings.md` carries editions, label structure, classification levels, and the ten ADatP-4778.2 binding profiles for 4774/4778/5636 — exactly the treatment §14's ACP 240 row names ("Findings extract in-repo; full text acquisition pending"). The STANAG row says "Not held" with no pointer. §14 is internally inconsistent about its own evidence.

6. §11 OpenTDF↔4778 survives, and the repo's own extract strengthens it: ADatP-4778.2's binding profiles are enumerated (REST, SOAP, XMPP, SMTP, Common XML Artefacts, Cryptographic Artefact Binding, XMP, Generic Open Packaging, OOXML, Sidecar) — all XML-schema-based, none of them TDF/ZTDF. §11 nonetheless lists "STANAG 4778 metadata binding" as one of four threads OpenTDF "converges". Whether ZTDF assertion binding satisfies any 4778 profile is an unverified external fact that the document asserts rather than schedules.

WHAT IS REFUTED:

- "…and ACP 240 as Authorities that … §14 records as 'Not held'". False. §14's ACP 240 row reads "Findings extract in-repo …; full text acquisition pending (operator)". ACP 240 is the one authority the corpus handles consistently and correctly across §2.1 (explicit conformance hedge), §13 Phase B ("ACP 240 gap analysis once the document is in hand"), §14, and D16 (which pairs the normative-guidance promotion with "§14 required-references list gates final design" — a hedge, not a bare promotion). The recommendation to "downgrade ACP 240 from Authority" should be dropped; ACP 240 is the model the other rows should be conformed TO.
- The stated cost driver on §11 ("expensive after the SDK API fossilizes") is weakened by D17: the crate "implements the OpenTDF spec, period" with zero Maknae coupling, so a 4778 shortfall would be an upstream/ecosystem question, not something Maknae's API fossilizes. The gap-analysis recommendation stands; the urgency framing does not.

SEVERITY: should-fix, unchanged. Nothing here is an enforcement defeat — no hook, lattice, or fail-closed property is wrong. It is verification-discipline/contract-honesty in a document explicitly badged "Draft — rough architecture" that already contains a §14 whose entire purpose is to make this gap explicit. It stays should-fix rather than nit because a security architecture that opens with "Verified … not model memory" and then contradicts itself two sections later damages the credibility of every other verified claim in the table, and because §14's stale STANAG row means the corpus is under-crediting evidence it actually holds. All fixes are prose: scope the preamble, extend the ACP 240 hedge verbatim to the other four, relabel the UIAS deliverable a placeholder, point §14's STANAG row at the in-repo extract, and move the OpenTDF↔4778 equivalence to §17.

findings.summary: 'The classic NIST AC-3/AC-4 decomposition' misattributes the PIP/PDP/PEP model: AC-3 and AC-4 are Access Enforcement and Information Flow Enforcement and define no such decomposition — it is SP 800-162's (and XACML's).
findings.evidence: Verified against SP 800-53r5: neither control nor its discussion introduces PIP/PDP/PEP roles. SP 800-162 is the document §14 lists as 'downloaded; lake ingestion pending', so the misattribution and the unread-source gap are the same gap. The provenance chain through the DoD ICAM RD's normative references is real; it is just pointed at the wrong NIST document.
findings.recommendation: Change to 'the standard ABAC decomposition (NIST SP 800-162; PIP/PDP/PEP/PAP), enforcing AC-3/AC-4' — which also lets §3 carry the PAP row it currently lacks even though §6.4's SPIF compilation is exactly a policy administration point.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
Verified against the text. `design/abac-dcs-architecture.md:60` (§3 opening) reads verbatim: "The classic NIST AC-3/AC-4 decomposition, mapped deliberately so anyone who knows the MCP reads Maknae, and vice versa:" followed by a table whose rows are PIP (subject), PIP (resource), PDP, PEP, at-rest backstop, presentation. That is the ABAC/XACML decomposition, and its NIST home is SP 800-162 (which defines PEP/PDP/PIP/PAP) — with SP 800-207 supplying the PE/PA/PEP variant. AC-3 (Access Enforcement) and AC-4 (Information Flow Enforcement) are SP 800-53r5 *controls*; neither the control statement nor its discussion introduces PIP/PDP/PEP roles. (I could not read an 800-53r5 catalog copy in this environment — local-ref-mat holds STIG/CCI material, not the catalog — but the control titles and the absence of a PIP/PDP/PEP decomposition in 800-53 are facts I hold with high confidence; if the panel wants a paper trail, this is the one external item to confirm on ingest.)

Refutation attempts, all failing:
1. Charitable reading — "the decomposition used to *implement* AC-3/AC-4." The sentence does not say that; it attributes the decomposition to AC-3/AC-4 as its source ("the classic NIST AC-3/AC-4 decomposition"). Notably the finding's own recommendation preserves this correct sense ("...enforcing AC-3/AC-4"), so the fix is a wording repair, not a claim reversal.
2. Corpus addresses it elsewhere. It does *not* cure it, and in fact convicts it: §2.1 line 34 correctly attributes PE/PA/PEP to SP 800-207, line 37 correctly attributes the ABAC definition to SP 800-162, and §15 line 327 uses AC-3/AC-4 correctly — as controls the three-layer enforcement *satisfies*. So the document elsewhere demonstrates it knows the right attribution; §3's opening is a local recall slip, and the surrounding correct usage makes the wrong one more confusing, not less.
3. Harmlessness. §2.1 opens with "Verified against the operator's knowledge lake (2026-07-15), not model memory" — this line, one section later, is a counterexample to that standing claim, and §14 lists SP 800-162 as "Downloaded; lake ingestion pending," i.e. the actual authority for this decomposition is the one document not yet read. Same gap, two symptoms, as the finding says. In a doc explicitly written for AI-agent consumption and destined to feed an RMF control narrative, a false authority attribution propagates.

The secondary observation is also true against the text: §3's table has no PAP row, while §6.4/§7.1 (line 182) state "The SPIF and the operator attribute store compile to Cedar entities at kernel load (ADR-0003's compilation contract)" and line 192 has RLS policies "generated from the SPIF" — that compilation/generation pipeline is a policy administration point in everything but name. Adding the row is an improvement, not an independent defect; I do not count it toward severity.

Severity held at should-fix rather than nit: the blast radius of the wording itself is zero (no design decision rests on it), but it is a false statement about a normative authority in a document that (a) claims lake-verification in the adjacent section and (b) carries a §15 control mapping that will be lifted into an RMF package. That is the same failure mode RL#1 recorded at #55–58 (maknae's summary of ADR-0004 drifting from the actual ADR text), which the review treated as gate-worthy, not cleanup-list.

findings.summary: 334KB of another system's internal design record is already committed to a repo intended to go public — including a live deployment's full operational security baseline and a coalition tetragraph whose membership the source itself marks '(classified)' — with the removal decision 'open' and no publication gate defined.
findings.evidence: references/oauth-compliance.md §6 is a complete deployment baseline for a different, live system: password policy, session and token lifespans, brute-force lockout settings, client IDs and scope grants, Terraform evidence paths, an internal address, a security contact, and issue/epic numbers. references/dcs-schema-migration.md §14 publishes '| NKIC | North Korea Intelligence Coalition | (classified) | No |' alongside a UNC/CFC information-sharing analysis. Neither is necessarily unreleasable; both are exactly what a pre-publication review exists to adjudicate. The defect is that no review is scheduled, no gate blocks the push, and the artifacts default to present — inverting the document's own fail-closed doctrine at the one boundary where the corpus itself is the data.
findings.recommendation: Convert the open decision into a gate: a §17 open question with a named owner and a decision-by milestone tied to the public push; a pre-publication content review of all three imports specifically adjudicating the oauth-compliance §6 baseline and the NKIC row with the source's owner; and, if reviewer access must be preserved, a pinned private submodule or an excerpt limited to what §5.1/§6.1 actually cite.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Verified directly against the text. (1) The imports are committed: design/references/ is 328K in three files, added by commits b41a9d0 and 7264110. (2) oauth-compliance.md §6 is a complete operational baseline for a different, live system — §6.2 password policy (15-char min, 24-generation history, 60-day expiry), §6.3 session/token lifespans (15-min SSO idle, 12-hour max, 5-min access token, 1-min auth code), §6.4 brute-force settings (5 failures, 30-min lockout, 12-hour reset), §6.6 named client IDs with per-client scope grants, and a Terraform evidence table (terraform/keycloak/{realm,clients,scopes}.tf). It also carries a security contact (security@securitymcp.io, lines 28 and 966), real internal FQDNs (mcp.cloud.darkhonor.net / auth.cloud.darkhonor.net, lines 304-305 — distinct from the example.com placeholders used elsewhere in the same file), ~20 Story/Epic numbers with deployment dates, and names its source as a private GitLab repo (gitlab.com/homelab-systems/security-mcp-server, line 4). (3) dcs-schema-migration.md line 1196 does contain the NKIC row verbatim, with lines 948/961/985 adding "member list is classified" and "DIA-sponsored". (4) The gate genuinely does not exist: §18 revision 0.2 records only "retention before public release is an open decision" — in a revision-history cell, with no owner and no milestone — and §17 Open questions holds 7 items (KAS placement, bulk-decision API, connection architecture, credential envelope, audit ceiling, TDF wrapping scope, Rust SDK scope), none of which is the retention decision. Nothing in README.md, the other design docs, or a .gitignore addresses it. Refutation attempts failed: the corpus does not handle this elsewhere; the public-release premise is the document's own phrasing, corroborated by README's namespace survey and TBD license; and this is not a YAGNI exclusion since the material is third-party content already imported wholesale. One partial refutation does land but is not fatal: the NKIC row withholds the classified membership rather than disclosing it, and whether the tetragraph's existence plus DIA sponsorship is itself releasable is an external fact unverifiable here — but the oauth §6 half alone establishes the defect without it. Severity revised down from blocker: the repo is currently PRIVATE (gh repo view: isPrivate true), so the exposure is latent and the trigger is a deliberate, unscheduled operator push; measured against RL#1's blocker bar (architecture-defeating defects B1-B22) this is release hygiene on companion refs, not an architecture defeat. It is a should-fix that escalates to blocker the moment a public push is scheduled.

(1) design/abac-dcs-architecture.md §14 (lines 307-319) is titled "References required before final design" and contains only a table of EXTERNAL documents to acquire (ACP 240, NIST SP 800-162/800-205/NISTIR 8112, ICTS UIAS, STANAG texts, CNSSI 1253, OpenTDF spec). findings.rl1_disposition: open — same root as RL#1 B10 (Class D, review line 94, routed to ADR-0008): the uniform max/union high-water join applied to a dimension where it is semantically wrong. B10 caught the antitone-releasability direction; this is the same root at a new seam in the opposite direction (a join can never exceed its inputs). ADR-0008 is still only proposed, so nothing has killed or relocated the class — the redesign under review has additionally hardened the wrong model into doctrine (§1.3) and into a CI property (§12). Not "new"; resurfaced.
findings.relocated_class: RL#1 Class D (MLS/BLP label-model gap) — B10's "uniform lattice join as the sole derivation model" root, resurfacing from KLC §6/§15 into abac-dcs-architecture §1 doctrine 3, §6.3, and §12. Same structural shape (one join rule for every label dimension), new seam; fold into ADR-0008 rather than tracking separately.
findings.summary: Doctrine 3 asserts as sound-by-construction that 'all-unrestricted inputs yield an unrestricted object' and §12 hard-codes it as a lattice-join property test, but the schema being ported explicitly supports classification-by-compilation, where individually unclassified items compile to a classified whole — and an agent assembling context from N retrievals is the compilation machine.
findings.evidence: A lattice join is by definition incapable of producing a result above every input. The imported source is explicit (E.O. 13526 §1.7(e), ISOO Notice 2017-02) and carries is_compilation and compilation_basis columns, neither of which appears in §6.1's port inventory; it also notes the guardrail Maknae has no analogue for — 'compilation classification is an OCA decision, not an automated determination'. In the origin a human curator marked documents; in Maknae §8.1's flow is automated multi-source assembly with no human determination and no representation for the outcome. Committing the join property to CI makes this expensive to unwind. (The source also contradicts itself on where the two columns live — §5a.4 says data tables, §24 defers them to confidentiality_labels.)
findings.recommendation: Either state explicitly that Maknae's derivation model is join-only and classification-by-compilation is an accepted, documented residual outside the threat model — a legitimate external-floor candidate that must be argued, with the operator-facing consequence stated — or port is_compilation/compilation_basis with an operator/OCA-in-the-loop path that can raise a context row above its join, restating the §12 property as 'join is the floor, not the value'.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Verified in the text. abac-dcs-architecture.md:23 (doctrine 3) states "all-unrestricted inputs yield an unrestricted object" as an unqualified property of the derived object; :154 (§6.3) says context rows are "born labeled at the join (lattice max)" — the value, not a floor; :293 (§12) commits "high-water-mark derivation is a lattice join" as a proptest. references/dcs-schema-migration.md:541-562 is explicit and authoritative-sourced (E.O. 13526 §1.7(e), ISOO Notice 2017-02): individually unclassified items may compile to a classified whole, with is_compilation/compilation_basis columns and the guardrail that compilation is an OCA decision. A lattice join cannot express this. The string "compilation" in the classification sense appears nowhere in abac-dcs-architecture.md, knowledge-lifecycle-contract.md, or container-architecture.md; §6.1's inventory echoes the source's own §24 column list (:1865, :2005) with "compilation flags" dropped. The consequence is reachable, not theoretical: KLC :102 routes at hook E on the payload high-water mark, so an assembled context whose join is UNCLASS but which an OCA would deem classified routes to an endpoint accredited only at the join and persists/replicates at that mark. §8.2's notional MPE SECRET//REL enclave plus the full SAP/SCI/coalition port put this inside the declared threat model, so YAGNI/deny-by-default does not excuse it. Two sub-claims are partially refuted and narrow the finding without killing it: (1) "neither column appears in §6.1's port inventory" overstates — §6.1 opens with "The complete dcs schema ... ports", so the columns arguably port under the completeness claim and the real gap is semantic (no derivation path, no doctrine, no operator/OCA-in-the-loop seam), not schematic; (2) "the source contradicts itself (§5a.4 data tables vs §24 labels)" is a stale-comment nit, not an open contradiction — D35/Q11 (:3568, :3602) explicitly adjudicate the flag onto confidentiality_labels only and say "Resolves Q11." Also, "expensive to unwind" is overstated: the §12 property constrains derivation, and the recommended restatement ("join is the floor, not the value") leaves it intact; the costly item is doctrine 3's soundness claim, which is a one-line fix now.

findings.section: §6.1 'Full DCS schema port' inventory vs references/dcs-schema-migration.md §23, §24
findings.rl1_disposition: open — an unaddressed instance of RL#1's Class B (two-representations drift), governed by redesign 0006 (single source of truth; point, don't restate). No redesign has been attempted at this seam, so it is neither killed nor relocated.
findings.summary: The §6.1 inventory is a prose restatement of the companion schema that does not match it: it omits Phase-A columns and tables the source defines (classification_system, originating_nation, handling_caveats, national_caveats, gdpr_applies/privacy_framework, cui_categories, nation_codes, coalition_members), claims a label_id placeholder and atomic-energy/SAP/SCI/declass fields the source defers or defines differently, and conflates §5a marking-policy analysis with the STANAG 4774 confidentiality_labels structure.
findings.evidence: The load-bearing omission is classification_system ('enables per-row disambiguation in multinational environments'), which interacts with §4 rule 4's one-lattice-per-deployment ruling: under one lattice there is no per-row framework variance, so the 14-framework registry §6.1 does port has no stated consumer, while the column that would have made it answerable is dropped. label_id belongs to confidentiality_labels, which the migration's own 'Does NOT' list defers to Phase B. §6.1 also restates the companion inventory while declaring it does not re-argue it — a second vocabulary list that can drift field-by-field.
findings.recommendation: Replace the prose inventory with a generated/checkable list diffed against the source migration in CI, or reconcile explicitly: port the missing columns and name their consumers, or state that one-lattice-per-deployment makes them unnecessary and that the classification_systems registry is ported solely as the SPIF equivalency-map source. Correct the confidentiality_labels attribution and the label_id phase.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
CONFIRMED ONLY IN NARROWED FORM. I verified §6.1 (abac-dcs-architecture.md:137) against the canonical column list in references/dcs-schema-migration.md §22 (lines ~1946–2005) and §1 (lines 124–151). Most of the finding's specific evidence is misread; a smaller real defect survives.

SURVIVING (verified): the migration's canonical "Column Definitions (Applied to Each Table)" block defines Phase-A data-table columns that §6.1's self-described "complete"/"Full" inventory silently omits: `originating_nation`, `handling_caveats`, `gdpr_applies`, `privacy_framework`, and `classification_system` (D36, "Enables per-row disambiguation in multinational environments"). That is a genuine instance of Class B two-representations drift — a prose restatement standing beside the artifact it claims to port.

REFUTED sub-claims (each checked against the text):
1. "label_id belongs to confidentiality_labels, deferred to Phase B" — FALSE. Migration §1 item 14 is explicit: "Adds nullable `label_id` FK placeholder for future STANAG 4774 labels" in *this* migration, and `label_id UUID DEFAULT NULL` appears in the Phase-A column block. §6.1's "STANAG 4774 `label_id` placeholder" is exactly correct.
2. "conflates §5a marking-policy analysis with the confidentiality_labels structure" and "claims atomic-energy/SAP/SCI/declass fields the source defers or defines differently" — FALSE. Every §5a SQL block is itself annotated "(on confidentiality_labels table, Phase B)", and the §22 note enumerates the same deferral list. §6.1's "atomic-energy/SAP/SCI and declassification fields (Phase B `confidentiality_labels`)" mirrors the source's own attribution, not a divergence.
3. "omits ... cui_categories, nation_codes, coalition_members" — FALSE. §6.1 names "CUI columns (categories, specified flag, the complete NARA LDC vocabulary, DI-block fields)" and "(GENC trigraphs + coalition tetragraph tables)".
4. "national_caveats" — not a defined column in the migration's canonical column block at all; it appears only as an illustrative cell in the §13 partner-caveat discussion table. Not an omission of a defined artifact.

REFUTED LOAD-BEARING ARGUMENT: the finding's blocker rationale is that "the 14-framework registry §6.1 does port has no stated consumer" under §4 rule 4's one-lattice-per-deployment ruling. §6.4 (line 158) already names the consumer verbatim: the SPIF is "levels, category sets, releasability communities, handling domains, **equivalency maps**" — the equivalency map is precisely the cross-framework consumer, and it is a boot-time-compiled Tier-0 artifact, not a per-row column. The finding's own recommended remedy ("state that the classification_systems registry is ported solely as the SPIF equivalency-map source") is substantially already in the document. With one lattice + an equivalency map at the SPIF, omitting a per-row `classification_system` FK is a defensible design position, not an unexplained gap — though §6.1 should say so rather than leave it silent.

FURTHER WEAKENING: the source itself is internally inconsistent on the phase of `classification_system` — §1 item 12 puts the FK column in Phase A, while decision D17 (line 3550) says the registry "enables `classification_system` column on labels (**Phase B**)". Likewise `is_compilation`/`compilation_basis` are marked "(on data tables)" in §5a but listed as Phase-B-deferred in the §22 note. An architecture summary cannot be held to blocker severity for failing to reproduce a source that disagrees with itself.

SEVERITY: not a blocker. §6.1 explicitly declares the companion canonical ("Design rationale imports by reference ... this document does not re-argue it"), and §6.2 declares the *implementation* source as generated `maknae-dcs-core` types, not this prose — so nothing normative is built from the inventory. The residual is a should-fix documentation seam: the paragraph advertises completeness ("Full", "The complete `dcs` schema", "Inventory:") while enumerating a lossy subset. The correct fix is the RL#1 §0006 redesign already on the books — point at the source instead of restating it (e.g. "ports the complete Phase-A column set defined in references/dcs-schema-migration.md §22", plus a one-line note on which Phase-A columns Maknae deliberately drops and why, e.g. classification_system superseded by the SPIF equivalency map). The finding's CI-diff recommendation is over-engineering for prose; deleting the second representation is cheaper and is what the corpus's own READ-reality doctrine prescribes.

SEPARATE DEFECT NOTICED (not this finding, worth filing): §6.3 lists "Handling caveats — `no-egress`, `operator-only`, enforced at hooks B/E" as a Maknae addition, while the migration's `handling_caveats TEXT` carries an explicit security note that it is "for **display purposes and NOT** [for ABAC]" (line 870, decision D5: "informational only, not for ABAC"). Same field name, opposite enforcement semantics, no reconciliation stated — a real Class B collision the reviewed finding missed while chasing an omission list.

findings.rl1_disposition: open (Class-A-adjacent, not a killed or relocated instance) — no corpus text addresses the writer or the value-domain mapping; unresolved as of this review
findings.relocated_class: imported-mechanism-semantics-mismatch: ported enum whose value domain models a foreign ingest model, with no populating path in the importing system (adjacent to RL#1 Class A via the unspecified write path, but not an instance of enforcement-without-a-locus)
findings.summary: classification_confidence is inventoried as a ported MCP column and made the basis of §10's spillage detection, but the imported migration never defines it — and its origin semantics (EXPLICIT / INFERRED / DEFAULT) are all unreachable or constant under Maknae's own ingest rules, so the detector cannot fire.
findings.evidence: 'DEFAULT' is unrepresentable by construction (unlabeled content is rejected; labels are NOT NULL; §9.2 'rejected, never defaulted'); 'INFERRED' names a DISA-filename-prefix parser Maknae has no analogue for; 'EXPLICIT' means human-assigned while Maknae's internally born rows are machine-derived at the high-water mark. The source itself records the control as only partly closed ('a formal Data Spillage Detection and Response section is still needed before Phase C').
findings.recommendation: Verify the column exists in the source; if not, declare it a Maknae extension and define its semantics. Re-map its value domain to Maknae's actual provenance classes (operator-declared / derived-at-join / imported-under-signature / imported-unverified) or drop it and state what actually detects spillage — most plausibly the KLC provenance/lineage axis. Do not leave §10's response chained to a detector that cannot fire.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
HALF-REFUTED, HALF-CONFIRMED — I verified both directions against the text, and the finding's headline claim is factually wrong.

REFUTED (the load-bearing premise): "the imported migration never defines it" is false. `design/references/dcs-schema-migration.md` §24 defines the column verbatim at lines 1987–1992:
  `classification_confidence VARCHAR(20)   DEFAULT 'DEFAULT',`
  `-- 'EXPLICIT' = human-assigned classification`
  `-- 'INFERRED' = derived from DISA filename prefix (U_, CUI_, etc.)`
  `-- 'DEFAULT'  = schema default (UNCLASSIFIED) — not yet assessed`
It is further carried in the migration-impact table (line 1850), decision D48 (line 3581), Q27 (line 3618), and DSAWG-F05 (line 3241–3249). abac §6.1 imports that companion by reference explicitly ("Design rationale imports by reference to … §4–§22; this document does not re-argue it"), so "ported column with no source" does not survive. The class label `ported-mechanism-with-no-source` is therefore wrong, and the "verify the column exists in the source" recommendation is already answered.

CONFIRMED (the residue, which I verified myself): the *value domain* does not map onto Maknae's own ingest/provenance model, and no populating path exists anywhere in the Maknae corpus.
- `'DEFAULT'` is the SQL column default and the source's semantics are "not yet assessed." Maknae §9.2 makes unassessed rows unrepresentable ("Object missing required labels at ingest | Rejected, never defaulted"; "State-store row without labels | Unrepresentable: NOT NULL label columns"). So the column defaults every row to a value whose meaning Maknae has designed out. With no writer specified, the failure is not "the detector cannot fire" (the finding's phrasing) but the opposite and worse: every row silently reads `'DEFAULT'` and the §10 detector fires on 100% of rows — pure noise chained to quarantine/purge machinery.
- `'INFERRED'` is defined as a DISA-filename-prefix parse; nothing in KLC §6/§7.2/§10 or abac §6.3 performs that parse, so the value is unreachable.
- `'EXPLICIT'` = "human-assigned," but abac §6.3 states internally born rows are machine-derived: "session/context rows are born labeled at the join (lattice max) of everything retrieved into them (hook C)." KLC §11.1 / §8 hook C likewise derive classification at the high-water mark under a derived-only lock. A high-water-mark-derived label is neither human-assigned, nor DISA-prefix-inferred, nor a schema default — Maknae's dominant provenance class has no value in the ported domain.
- The source itself is accurately quoted as only partly closing the control (line 3247: "a formal §28d 'Data Spillage Detection and Response' section … is still needed before Phase C"), so abac §10's flat assertion "`classification_confidence` flags suspect rows" over-claims relative to its own cited authority.

So: the column exists and is sourced; what is missing is (a) any Maknae-side writer, and (b) a value domain re-mapped to Maknae's actual provenance classes (operator-declared / derived-at-join / imported-under-signature). The finding's recommendation is right in its second half only.

SEVERITY: downgraded blocker → should-fix. It is not a blocker because (i) the "no source" premise is false, (ii) abac §6.1's import-by-reference is a legitimate, explicitly-scoped delegation, and (iii) the residual is a defined, local seam — add a populating rule and re-map three enum values — not a structural redesign. It is not a nit because §10 chains a destructive response (quarantine/purge) to a signal that, as specified, is constant across all rows.

CLASS: the finding's Class A tag ("enforcement asserted without a locus") is only loosely apt — §10's response locus (KLC demotion machinery, state-store column) does exist; what is absent is the *writer* of the detector's input. That is Class-A-adjacent (an integrity-relevant field with an unspecified write path) but its truer shape is an imported-mechanism semantics mismatch: a ported enum whose value domain models a different system's ingest. It is a live instance, not a killed or relocated one — nothing in the corpus addresses it.

EXTERNAL FLOOR: no. Defining who writes the column and what its values mean under Maknae's provenance model is entirely inside the system's control.

findings.summary: DISPLAY ONLY and ORCON are no-retention / no-extraction controls; Maknae retains and derives from everything it retrieves by construction, so the columns are ported with no enforcement locus and no stated boundary.
findings.evidence: The source defines DISPLAY ONLY as 'disclosure without providing physical copies — foreign nationals may view but may NOT retain a copy' and ORCON as originator-controlled extraction. §8.1 assembles retrieved content into model context and §6.3 records that session rows are born labeled at the join of everything retrieved — i.e. the content is retained and an LLM response over it is a derivation. All three enforcement layers are visibility controls; none expresses 'may be seen but not retained or restated', and §8.2 never mentions DISPLAY ONLY. A human reading a screen can be told not to keep a copy; a context-assembly pipeline cannot.
findings.recommendation: Decide and record which: make DISPLAY-ONLY/ORCON-marked content ineligible for retrieval into agent context as a hook-B/hook-C deny predicate (the enforceable reading), or accept the residual explicitly as an argued external floor. Either way remove the implication that porting the column ports the control.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
Verified against text. Confirmed core: §6.1 (abac-dcs-architecture.md:137) ports `display_only_nations` and "classified dissemination controls" into the label vocabulary; the imported companion references/dcs-schema-migration.md §9 (lines 775-790) defines DISPLAY ONLY per DoDM 5200.01-V2 Encl.4 §10.e.(3) as "disclosure without providing physical copies ... may NOT retain a copy" and :520 defines ORCON as originator-controlled dissemination/extraction, while giving DISPLAY ONLY only a schema column and no enforcement semantics (its §10 "Schema Decision" reduces dissemination enforcement to `WHERE user_nationality = ANY(rel_to_nations)`, a pure visibility predicate). All three enforcement layers are row-visibility mechanisms: §7.1 Cedar decisions over labels, §7.2 PEP label-predicate injection, §7.3 RLS whose enumerated predicate set is "dominance predicate over the classification ordinal + releasability array containment + `noforn` + `subject`/`handling_grants` join". No retention or derivation predicate exists anywhere in the corpus. §6.3 confirms retention/derivation by construction ("session/context rows are born labeled at the join (lattice max) of everything retrieved into them (hook C)") and §8.1 assembles retrieved content into model context. §8.2 — the SECRET//REL coalition flow, the natural home for DISPLAY ONLY — enumerates NOFORN enforcement in detail and never mentions DISPLAY ONLY or ORCON; §12's vector spine lists only "releasability/handling/NOFORN cases"; §9.2, §15, §16 and §17 are silent.

PARTIAL REFUTATION (narrows the recommendation): the clause "remove the implication that porting the column ports the control" misreads §13. The Growth-path table scopes Phase A to "Full schema present (§6.1); core lattice + handling + subject scoping enforced at all three layers", defers "Coalition apparatus fully exercised (JOINT/FGI/tetragraph workflows)" to Phase C, and states the doctrine explicitly: "schema early on empty tables, apparatus activated when the consuming code exists." §6.5's certification gate is a second deliberate instance of schema-outruns-enforcement. The corpus therefore does not claim these controls are enforced.

SURVIVING DEFECT: §13's deferral presumes the apparatus can be activated later. Nothing records that DISPLAY ONLY's no-retention half and ORCON's no-extraction half are different in kind from everything the three-layer model can express — a visibility lattice cannot express "may be seen but not retained or restated," and §6.3's high-water-mark derivation guarantees retention of whatever is retrieved. A Phase-C implementer will discover this rather than find it decided, and an operator can today mark content DISPLAY ONLY, receive only a nation-visibility grant, and get no analogue of the §6.5 loud NOT-CERTIFIED warning. The recommendation's first half (hook-B/hook-C deny predicate, or an argued+recorded residual) is the right fix; the second half should be restated as "record that DISPLAY ONLY/ORCON have no expressible semantics in the three-layer model, rather than leaving them inside the generic §13 apparatus deferral."

findings.section: §4 (scoped task identities), §7.2 vs container-architecture.md §3.6 and references/dcs-schema-migration.md §28b
findings.relocated_class: RL#1 "identity-consumed-but-never-established" (digest B-class: subject/service identity is a decision input throughout the corpus — gateway asserts operator identity, scheduler mints scoped task identities, dreamer runs under a scoped identity — while the mechanism that establishes and populates it is stated nowhere). The §4 redesign kills this for OPERATOR principals (Tier-0 signed attribute store, kernel binds, no self-assertion, claims never the attribute source) but preserves the identical structural shape for TASK principals: "scoped task identities (scheduler, dreamer) are just subjects with narrow attribute sets" asserts the model without specifying attribute content, provisioning path, or per-subject vs corpus-wide operation. Symptom fixed for one principal class, shape retained for another = relocated, not killed. Second, narrower relocation: the label-composition class — the lattice axis got an explicit join rule (high-water mark), the `subject`/`handling_grants` ownership axis got none, so "derived-object labeling is unspecified" moved from the whole label to one axis of it.
findings.summary: The ported no-acknowledgement/RLS model assumes interactive per-user sessions, but the dreamer is an unattended batch consolidator whose job requires reading across subjects — and the redesign gives it one clause and no attribute model, leaving only two resolutions: it cannot do its job, or it is a cross-subject aggregation channel.
findings.evidence: §4's entire treatment is 'scoped task identities (scheduler, dreamer) are just subjects with narrow attribute sets', while §7.2's mechanism assumes session shape. container §3.6 defines the dreamer's work (dedup, corroboration, memory distillation) as inherently cross-corpus, and the corpus now includes per-operator, subject-scoped state-store rows. A dreamer with broad attributes reads every subject's rows and emits distilled memories labeled at the join of everything it read — aggregation plus label creep in the one identity that runs unattended.
findings.recommendation: Specify the dreamer's subject context concretely: which attributes it carries, whether it operates per-subject (N scoped passes that never join across operators — the shape that preserves the ported no-acknowledgement property) or corpus-wide, and what the label of its outputs is. If corpus-wide, name the mechanism preventing its outputs from becoming a cross-subject channel. Add the dreamer to §12's negative tests.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Verified against document text. REFUTED IN PART: (1) "§7.2's mechanism assumes session shape" is a misread — §7.2 says the subject context "is issued once per session/task", naming task identities explicitly. (2) "what the label of its outputs is" is largely answered — abac §6.3 ("High-water-mark derivation — session/context rows are born labeled at the join (lattice max) of everything retrieved into them (hook C)") and KLC line 101 ("a derived object classifies at the high-water mark of its inputs") specify the classification-axis label for exactly the dreamer's hook-C write path; label creep at the join is the intended mechanism, and it makes over-classified outputs a utility problem, not a disclosure channel. (3) The "cross-subject aggregation channel" horn is closed by default: abac §6.3 "cross-subject access is an explicit grant, deny by default"; KLC hook B "cross-persona memory access requires explicit rule"; KLC open-question #7 rescoped 2026-07-14 — "Deny-by-default already answers the MVP case — no rule means no cross-access — and `subject` scoping ships in the schema from birth". (4) The dreamer does not mount `state-data` (container §4: "no other container mounts it — access is SQL through layer-2 PEPs only"), so its state-store reads transit a kernel-minted subject context (§7.2) with RLS backstop (§7.3) — it has no unmediated path to per-operator rows. CONFIRMED RESIDUAL, narrowed: the corpus defines a composition rule for the lattice axis under derivation (join = lattice max) but defines NO composition rule for the `subject` / `handling_grants` ownership axis, which §6.3 lists as a bullet separate from high-water-mark derivation and which is not a lattice point. The unanswerable question against the text: what is the `subject` of a memory distilled from rows owned by operators A and B? High-water mark does not cover it; the deny-by-default grant rule governs reads, not the ownership label of derived writes. §4 gives the one unattended identity a single clause with no stated attribute posture, container §3.6 defines its job (dedup, corroboration, memory distillation) as inherently cross-corpus, and §12's negative tests include "cross-subject health query" but nothing for the dreamer. That is a real, ADR-worthy specification gap — a patchable seam, and one that fails closed rather than open in the default posture.

findings.summary: The origin migration deliberately defaults classification to UNCLASSIFIED and states parser/service code need not change because 'defaults handle everything'; porting it as 'not a new design' imports a fail-open bottom incompatible with Maknae's reject-unlabeled ingest rules, and the semantic break is never acknowledged.
findings.evidence: Origin: DEFAULT 'UNCLASSIFIED', 'does NOT require parser changes (existing imports continue unchanged)'. Maknae: 'unlabeled content is rejected', 'nothing is ever silently assumed open', 'label columns are NOT NULL', §9.2 'rejected, never defaulted'.
findings.recommendation: State explicitly in §6.1 that the port removes the UNCLASSIFIED default and requires explicit classification on ingest, document the semantic break from the origin, and add the rejecting validation to the write path and the §12 vectors.
findings.verifier_reasoning:
VERIFIED TEXT

Origin (design/references/dcs-schema-migration.md), quotes check out:
- L119: "| Parser changes | None (defaults handle everything) | …"
- L149: "Does NOT require parser changes (existing imports continue unchanged)"
- L127: classification_level ENUM "defaulting to 'UNCLASSIFIED' (D31)"
- L1948: `classification_level dcs.classification_level DEFAULT 'UNCLASSIFIED' NOT NULL,`
- L2049, L2188, L2209: "all data is UNCLASSIFIED", "all records are UNCLASSIFIED by default", "Phase A: Columns exist, all data is UNCLASSIFIED → no risk".

Maknae (design/abac-dcs-architecture.md §6.1): "The complete `dcs` schema from the MCP ports as Maknae's label vocabulary — this is a port of a built artifact, not a new design. … Design rationale imports by reference to the in-repo companion … §4–§22; this document does not re-argue it."

WHAT IS REFUTED (the majority of the finding as filed)

1. "Imports a fail-open bottom incompatible with Maknae's ingest rules, and the semantic break is never acknowledged" — the break IS acknowledged, explicitly and in the exact terms the finding demands, in three normative places:
   - §1 doctrine 3 (L23): "Nothing is ever *silently assumed* open; everything is *cheaply declared* open: external content declares its label at ingest (declaring the bottom is one line; unlabeled content is rejected, KLC §6)". This sentence exists precisely to distinguish "frictionless bottom" from "defaulted bottom".
   - §9.2 row: "Object missing required labels at ingest | Rejected, never defaulted (KLC §6…)".
   - KLC §6 ("rejected, not defaulted") + §15 invariant `missing_required_labels_at_ingest: reject`.
2. Recommendation items 3 and 4 are already satisfied: §6.4 compiles the SPIF into "Label validators (ingest and write-path schema enforcement)", and §12 states "every row of the §9.2 matrix becomes a test" — i.e. the rejecting validation and its vectors are already specified.
3. §6.1's scope is the label *vocabulary* (its inventory is ENUMs, columns, registries, the label_id placeholder), not the origin's migration posture; the companion carries an explicit read-only-snapshot import banner. And §2.2 already states the structural reason the origin's default cannot transfer: "Maknae builds it from birth on empty tables" — the origin default exists to avoid backfill/downtime on a live DB (L118–119), a condition Maknae does not have. So "blocker / fail-open ingest" is not sustainable.

WHAT SURVIVES (narrower, and I verified it myself)

The residual is a mechanism-claim error, not an ingest-doctrine break. §9.2 asserts: "State-store row without labels | Unrepresentable: `NOT NULL` label columns + deny-all default RLS policy." The ported DDL that §6.1 blanket-imports is `DEFAULT 'UNCLASSIFIED' NOT NULL` (L1948). Under that DDL an INSERT that omits classification_level does NOT error — it silently materializes a bottom-labeled row. NOT NULL alone therefore does not deliver the "unrepresentable" property §9.2 claims for it; NOT NULL *without* a DEFAULT does. An implementer following §6.1's instruction ("port of a built artifact… this document does not re-argue it") and copying the companion's column block ships a state store where the §9.2 guarantee is false at the DB layer, leaving only the application-layer validator — exactly the single-layer condition doctrine 1/§7.3's at-rest backstop exists to prevent. The corpus also has no precedence clause anywhere stating that the architecture document governs where an imported companion conflicts (grep for normative/precedence/conflict finds none), so nothing textually stops the copy.

Fix is one clause, not a redesign: §6.1 should state that the port takes the vocabulary and drops the origin's `DEFAULT 'UNCLASSIFIED'` (and `owner_nations '{USA}'` / `originating_nation 'USA'`, same shape), plus a general "where this document and an imported companion differ, this document governs" line; and the §12 vector for the §9.2 row must be written as "INSERT omitting the label column → error", which is the test that actually distinguishes the two DDLs.

CLASS

This is a fresh instance of RL#1's Class B (two representations of one fact that must agree), now at import scale: the companion is a second, unreconciled representation of the label model. RL#1's scope (§ header, corpus commit 5e76b96, dated 2026-07-14) does not include abac-dcs-architecture.md or references/ — those landed 2026-07-15 — so this is new, not a relocation of an RL#1 blocker. Nothing is relocated; the seam is patchable in the document, so no external floor.

Severity: should-fix. It is a real, checkable defect in a stated failure-mode guarantee, but it is contradicted by three normative statements elsewhere in the same corpus, so it cannot silently become the implementation's doctrine the way a blocker would.

findings.verifier_reasoning:
Verified against the text; confirmed but NARROWED — part of the finding is refuted by explicit phasing.

REFUTED PORTION: §13 Phase C explicitly defers "Coalition apparatus fully exercised (JOINT/FGI/tetragraph workflows)" under the stated doctrine "schema early on empty tables, apparatus activated when the consuming code exists" (the same schema-from-birth/apparatus-later pattern as the §6.5 certification gate). CONFIRMED RESIDUE (verified myself, three parts):
(1) §4 load-bearing rule 4 states "one lattice per deployment; subject attributes and resource labels are both points in it. The SPIF (§6.4) is the single vocabulary source." The §4 example then uses `communities: [REL-AUS, REL-KOR]` — a vocabulary appearing nowhere in the resource label model, which uses `rel_to_nations` over GENC trigraphs + tetragraphs (§6.1). findings.verifier_reasoning:
Verified directly against design/abac-dcs-architecture.md.

§5.1 (L114-125) adopts the MCP's 13-RFC record "wholesale" as Maknae's baseline. The list is topologically mixed: RS/client-implementable items (RFC 9068 validation, JOSE FIPS allowlist enforced twice, RFC 9728, RFC 9110/9111 startup URL validation, JWKS caching) sit undifferentiated alongside AS-only items — "RFC 7591 DCR + CIMD ... with policy fences (consent required, full-scope disabled, scope allowlists, client caps, TTL cleanup)", "refresh token rotation", RFC 8707 audience ISSUANCE, and RFC 8414 metadata publication.

§5.2.1 (L129) then declares "Maknae is never the Authorization Server" and defines the federation contract as "Maknae requires of the IdP exactly what the baseline requires: RFC 8414 discovery, PKCE S256, RFC 9068 tokens, FIPS-listed algorithms." That sentence is self-refuting inside the same document: the four-item list is a strict subset of §5.1 yet is asserted to BE the baseline. Most sharply, it omits the item §5.1 itself names "the critical anti-replay control" — RFC 8707. Maknae keeps 8707 validation ("mandatory and construction-guarded") but never requires the IdP to issue resource-indicator-bound audiences; in the MCP this required a Keycloak audience protocol mapper (references/oauth-compliance.md §3.5: "Implemented By | Keycloak (audience mapper) + security-gateway (audience validation)"). A §5.2-conforming IdP can therefore produce tokens that fail Maknae's mandatory audience check, or — if relaxed to a static aud — silently forfeit anti-replay. Refresh rotation and the 7591 fences are asserted as baseline with no owner across any of the three surfaces.

Refutation attempts, all failed:
(1) "The imported companion already maps implementers." It does — every RFC section carries an "Implemented By" row — but exclusively to the Keycloak-as-AS topology Maknae explicitly rejects. It supplies the NON-transferable mapping, which strengthens rather than discharges the finding.
(2) "YAGNI / out-of-surface is implied." Nothing in §5, §11 or §13 excludes AS-side items. §11 (L329) compounds the overclaim: "OAuth 2.1 identity front door (RFC baseline §5.1) | IA-2, IA-5(2), IA-8, SC-8, SC-13, SC-23" claims the whole control set for Maknae, though IA-5(2) is substantially IdP-side — a compliance overclaim heading into an ATO package. §13 D7 restates the same undifferentiated claim.
(3) "§5.2.2 covers CIMD." Only as an OAuth client; the 7591 policy fences stay ownerless.
(4) Cross-corpus grep for audience/refresh/rotation/consent/Resource Server across all three design docs plus the RL1 review: no implementer-surface assignment anywhere; "audience" (OAuth sense) occurs only at L119 and §12 open-question 4.

Severity re-assessed blocker -> should-fix. The architecture decision (never the AS; marry the RFC contract, not the IdP product) is sound and needs no redesign — so this does not block. But it exceeds presentation: the §5.2 IdP contract is missing a named security requirement (8707 issuance) whose absence has a concrete failure mode, plus an inherited NIST control overclaim. That is should-fix, not nit.

The finding's own class label holds and is worth keeping: this is the doctrine's two-representations/READ-reality family — the MCP compliance record was restated rather than pointed-to, and it has already drifted within a single document (§5.1 contradicts §5.2). The fix shape is the recommended per-surface mapping (require-of-IdP / implement-as-RS / implement-as-client) with AS-only assertions separated out and folded into the §5.2 federation contract.

(1) abac-dcs-architecture.md:118 sits under §5.1 "Adopted wholesale from the MCP's compliance record," with exactly one annotated divergence (aws-lc-rs vs BoringCrypto) — so the inherited implementation semantics port unchanged by the doc's own framing. (c) External floor — no; the reference implementation already performs the discovery fetch at boot (discovery.go / ValidatePKCESupport), so converting WARN to refuse-to-serve is a seam entirely under Maknae's control.

Severity stays should-fix, not blocker: exploitation requires an operator to federate a non-conforming IdP AND an authorization-code interception path; the residual is a real but bounded misconfiguration-tolerance gap rather than a direct bypass of the ABAC/BLP model.
